name: Ab Wheel Rollout — Kneeling
description: The kneeling ab wheel rollout is a highly effective anti-extension core exercise in which the athlete rolls a wheel forward from a kneeling position while resisting lumbar hyperextension through maximal core bracing. The movement recruits the transverse abdominis, rectus abdominis, and latissimus dorsi isometrically and eccentrically in a coordinated chain, training the core's ability to resist spinal extension forces — a fundamental quality for athletic performance and injury prevention.

execution.starting_position: Kneel on the floor with knees hip-width apart. Grip the ab wheel handles and position the wheel directly under the shoulders.
execution.setup_instructions: Place a mat under the knees for comfort. Keep the hips at roughly a 90° angle to start.
steps: Step 1: Brace the core fully. Begin rolling the wheel forward slowly.
Step 2: Extend the arms overhead as the torso lowers toward the floor, maintaining a straight line from knees through hips to shoulders.
Step 3: Roll out as far as can be controlled without the lower back arching.
Step 4: Pull the wheel back toward the knees using the lats and abs simultaneously.
Step 5: Return to the starting position and repeat.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before rolling out. Exhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Allowing the hips to drop and the lumbar spine to hyperextend during the rollout
Not engaging the lats on the pullback — leads to arm-only return
safety_considerations: Regress to a shorter range of motion if back pain occurs
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Roll out until hips begin to drop — that is the individual limit. Build range gradually.
coaching_cues: Squeeze the abs like you're about to be punched
Pull the wheel back with your lats — elbows to hips
